clue.text: A farmer finally fit, fit for ploughing

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows, so only its end is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of farmer
fit in the sense of capable

explanation.surface: A farmer at last in good health, and the field ready to be ploughed.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'fit' is the trick: the first is the wordplay, the second starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is land suitable for growing crops, which means land that can be ploughed.

clue.text: Wanting marriage, daughter drops out of amorous relationship

indicators.note: something that drops out of a thing is no longer in it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a dalliance is a casual love affair

explanation.surface: A daughter who wants to get married walks away from a mere fling.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the D off the front of DALLIANCE. 'Wanting' only sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union, and in older usage it often means a marriage between families.

clue.text: A female, articulate and rich

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
an articulate speaker is a fluent one

explanation.surface: A description of a well-spoken, wealthy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent is a direct synonym meaning wealthy or well off.

clue.text: Big freight vessel left for Britain

indicators.note: X for Y means one letter takes the place of another in the word

blocks.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat carrying goods
L is the abbreviation for left
B is the abbreviation for Britain

explanation.surface: A huge cargo ship has departed for the UK.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left for Britain' looks like a sailing; it means L replaces B at the start of BARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Large is a plain synonym of big, both describing considerable size.

clue.text: Property propositions

blocks.note: first meaning: a building with its land
second meaning: statements an argument is based on

explanation.walkthrough: The two words alliterate as if one phrase about property deals, but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a house or building with grounds and the starting assumptions of a logical argument.

clue.text: So marry her, one moved, displaying logic

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters have been shifted out of their original places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, emotionally moved, decides to marry her, and this is offered as sound reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is normally used in the negative: something with no rhyme or reason makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme or reason means sense or rational explanation, which is what logic supplies.

clue.text: A fellow, surrounded by kinky US dames, complained

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order
something surrounded by another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man among some kinky American ladies had cause to object.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange US DAMES as MADE USS, then put A F into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a fuss is to protest or grumble loudly, so made a fuss means complained.

clue.text: Read about king, well-built

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Read up on a monarch who was strongly built.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means strongly made and robust, the same as solidly constructed.

clue.text: Circle province

blocks.note: first meaning: a social set or group of people
second meaning: an area of activity or influence

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look geographic or geometric, but each is a sense of a word that also means a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere can be a social circle, and also a field of influence or province, as in sphere of interest.

clue.text: Cry of lady swimming in a residential enclave in Nassau

indicators.note: swimming letters float about and come back in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman calls out while swimming at an exclusive Bahamas resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas; a cay is a small low island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyford Cay is a gated, wealthy private community on the western tip of New Providence island near Nassau.

clue.text: American rustic - fine example by pub on line

blocks.note: a cracker is an excellent specimen of something
a bar serves drinks like a pub
re means on or concerning
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A fine specimen of a country type sits by a pub on a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'cracker' is something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US, cracker-barrel describes homespun, folksy country wisdom, from the barrel of crackers in old general stores.

clue.text: Bread, and what's used to make it

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for money
second meaning: the kneaded mixture baked into a loaf

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Bread' as food, but in the first meaning it is slang for cash, which is also this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for money, like bread, and is also the flour-and-water mix that a loaf is baked from.

clue.text: A charming French accent

blocks.note: taken as written
cute means attractively charming

explanation.surface: Someone finds a French way of speaking charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French accent' sounds like a way of speaking; it is a written mark, as on é.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is the rising diacritic mark used in French over the letter e, an accent in the typographic sense.

clue.text: Boy, a youth who drowned saving ten

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe, here holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
in Greek myth Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach Hero
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A young man drowned while rescuing ten people.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that Leander drowned saving no one; he was swimming to his lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander is a boy's given name, so it is an example of a boy in crossword terms.

clue.text: Irritable about intelligence surrounding large ship

indicators.note: surrounding means placed all around, so one word is wrapped about another

blocks.note: CA, short for circa, means about
nous is common sense or intelligence
a tanker is a big ship carrying oil

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy about how smart a big ship is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the container signal, but it is circa; 'surrounding' does that job. Nous is a British word for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means bad-tempered and argumentative, which is a stronger synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Maturity shown by a deckhand originally guarding hold out at sea

indicators.note: originally refers to the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
at sea means in confusion, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of deckhand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor shows a grown-up attitude keeping watch over the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guarding' only places A and D in front of the rearranged letters; nothing goes inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulthood is the state of being fully grown, which is what maturity means.

clue.text: Harshly criticise article on a building that was built to honour gods

definitions.text: a building that was built to honour gods

blocks.note: to pan is to review scathingly
the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic attacks an essay about a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link meaning 'about', but it is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome was a temple dedicated to all the gods; the word now names any such temple.

clue.text: Bid to imprison complete delinquent

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock someone inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a bid is an offer
to complete is to end

explanation.surface: An attempt to lock up an utter wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like an adjective for the delinquent; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is a person who breaks the law, the same as a delinquent used as a noun.

clue.text: Old English weapon found in barracks by Welsh river

blocks.note: quarters are soldiers' lodgings
the Taff flows through Cardiff

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon is discovered in an army base beside a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like a container signal, but the pieces simply join.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarterstaff is a long wooden pole used as a weapon by English peasants, as wielded by Little John.

clue.text: When this is not shown, old lady makes a complaint

indicators.note: what is not shown is left out, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: as can mean when
taken as written
the letters removed from the previous word
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman grumbles when something is kept from her.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop IS from THIS to leave TH. 'Old lady' is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a medical condition of the airways, and complaint is a common word for an illness.

clue.text: Kind offer

blocks.note: first meaning: gentle and caring
second meaning: a formal bid, or to present

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a generous offer, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender is an adjective for gentle and loving, and also a noun or verb for a formal offer, as in a business tender.

clue.text: Dropped charges causing one to cry

blocks.note: to shed is to let fall or drop
to tear is to rush or charge along

explanation.surface: Criminal charges are withdrawn and a defendant weeps with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped charges' reads as a legal phrase; here both are verbs, the second meaning rushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed tears is to let tears fall, which is what crying is.

clue.text: One identifies bishop and rook pocketed by child

indicators.note: something pocketed by another is put inside it

blocks.note: a mite is a small child
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A child spots a bishop and a rook on a chessboard and pockets the rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop and rook' suggests chess; the bishop belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed headdress worn by bishops is their distinctive emblem, so it marks out a bishop.

clue.text: Animal lows close to byre

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: a cow lows, that is, moos
the last letter of byre

explanation.surface: A beast bellows near a cowshed.
explanation.walkthrough: A byre is a cowshed. 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it picks the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large North American deer, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Some characters in healthy Droitwich spa

indicators.note: some of the letters inside the following words make up the solution

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Droitwich, a healthy spa town, has some interesting characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Droitwich is an English spa town in Worcestershire, which makes 'spa' look like part of the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a British word for a hotel or resort offering water cures, a type of spa.

clue.text: Deteriorate? Manage to consult foremost of doctors

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to manage a business is to run it
taken as written
to see a doctor is to consult one
the first letter of doctors

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell? Try to get an appointment with the leading doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: To run to seed is to decline in condition, as a plant does after flowering, so it means to deteriorate.

clue.text: Beginning to ask one about new lead for dog

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
something new is made afresh, so these letters are given a different order

blocks.note: the first letter of ask
I is the Roman numeral for one
re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Starting to ask someone about a new leash for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is a dog lead, or leash, in the surface; in the wordplay its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: Note from voice on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are only heard, so we go by how the word sounds

blocks.note: a tenor is a high male singing voice

explanation.surface: A note sung by a singer on a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music; it is a banknote. A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenner is British slang for a ten-pound banknote, so it is a kind of note.
